newsitem.title: HUNGARY: OMV Hungary unit boosts '96 sales by 40pct.
newsitem.headline: OMV Hungary unit boosts '96 sales by 40pct.

text.p: The Hungarian subsidiary of Austrian oil firm OMV boosted its turnover by 40 percent to 36 billion forints in 1996, OMV Hungaria Kft said on Tuesday.

OMV Hungaria managing director Tamas Mayer told a news conference that the acqusition of 31 filling stations from Kuwait Petroleum last year, almost doubling the company's network, was a main factor behind the growth.
OMV said it planned a further increase in turnover to 47 billion forints this year, and to expand its retail market share to nine percent by 2000 from 7.7 percent in 1996.
OMV's market share in central eastern Europe is over 10 percent, OMV said in a statement.

Mayer said OMV Hungaria posted a loss of some 550 million forints last year due to investments and because Hungarian oil company MOL, the market leader in Hungary, kept trade margins at about half the average Austrian level.
"We hope that in 1998, our annual result will be positive," he added.
